title: A quiet night in the cellar
text: Only one brewer's cart rumbled overhead. Everyone slept well despite the smell of damp.

title: Rats in the larder
text: A swarm of rats got into the flour sacks. By the time they were chased off, a good share of the stores was gone.

title: A drunken brawl next door
text: Two guild masters beat each other up over spirits in the next tenement. The watch came, but down the wrong alley.

title: A dropped purse
text: A purse lay on the doorstep in the morning, lost by someone in a hurry. There's no name in it, only some silver.

title: Bells of Morr at midnight
text: The chapel bells of Morr rang for no reason. Some of the crew didn't sleep until dawn.

title: A merchant without guards
text: A drunk merchant lost his way in the alley and asked for the inn. No one touched him, but a few looked greedily.

title: Free bread
text: To mark a holy day the baker handed out yesterday's loaf to anyone in the queue. The crew queued three times.

title: Smoke from the hearth
text: The chimney drew badly and the whole den filled with smoke. By morning everyone was coughing and complaining of headaches.

title: Quarrel over a blanket
text: Two followers argued over the last dry blanket. The chief ruled in Solomon's manner, taking the blanket himself.

title: The town crier
text: A town crier shouted about new taxes and wanted lists under the window. Some of the news was particularly interesting.

title: A strange flask
text: Someone left a flask of cheap spirits on the sill with a note, "To your health." Nobody owned up to it.

title: The cat on the roof
text: A ginger cat crept onto the roof and chased pigeons all night. In the morning it laid one at the threshold like a gift.

title: The chimney sweep
text: A chimney sweep came down the flue straight onto a follower's lap. They both shrieked until everyone woke.

title: Patrol under the window
text: The watch passed under the window three times. The crew kept quiet, but more than one lost their nerve.

title: A late delivery
text: The carter brought the ordered supplies only after dark and demanded a surcharge. It was paid, but without a smile.

title: Singing from the inn
text: From the inn across the street came old songs about Sigmar and the lasses of the Reikland. Some went to listen.

title: The night hawker
text: At dawn a pickle seller stood at the door. He haggled fiercely but left with an empty basket.

title: A priestess of Shallya
text: A priestess of Shallya with a basket of herbs knocked for alms. She got some coppers and blessed everyone.

title: Burning basket
text: A basket of rubbish caught fire somewhere in the alley. People ran out with buckets while the crew quietly tidied up what it could.

title: A strange light in a window
text: A greenish light flickered in the window opposite all night. Imagination or an alchemist, nobody wanted to guess.

title: Wedding in the tenement
text: The whole tenement was celebrating a baker's lad's wedding. The crew got leftover cake and a few mugs of ale.

title: Night storm
text: A storm flooded the alleys ankle-deep, but the den stayed dry and the rain drowned any traces.

title: A Witch-Hunter's handbill
text: Someone slid a handbill under the door listing those suspected of heresy. Two of the names were familiar.

title: A suspicious neighbour
text: The neighbour across the way has been staring at your door too much all week. He surely has some business, but what?

title: Orphans singing
text: Children from a Shallyan foundling home sang under the windows for bread. Nobody had the heart to shoo them away.

title: The grain merchant
text: Grain has gone up in the city and the merchant who usually supplied you now wants more. You have to adapt.

title: A pigeon with a letter
text: A pigeon landed on the sill with a note on its leg. The letter wasn't for you, but it carried interesting information.

title: The old washerwoman's curse
text: The washerwoman in the yard loudly cursed the whole crew because someone trampled her laundry. Nobody knows if it means anything.

title: Fire in the next street
text: A fire broke out nearby. The city watch ran off that way, leaving the streets under your control.

title: A wrecked wagon
text: A cart of barrels overturned outside your door. A few barrels rolled into the cellar, nobody knows how.

title: An amateur thief
text: A lad from the next street tried to rob you. Caught, he burst into tears and told you all about his own affairs.

title: A drunk bruiser at the door
text: A drunk bruiser from the city guard pounds on the door demanding a "tenants' tax." Without a proper response it'll turn into trouble.
okText: The bodyguard stepped out, gave him one look and the bruiser left, leaving his own coins behind.

title: The guild collector
text: A guild debt collector came for the overdue cellar rent, with two burly henchmen.
okText: The bodyguard stood in the doorway and politely explained that nobody was home today.

title: A shadow on your tail
text: Someone has been following crew members for several evenings. He must be shaken off or caught before he reveals the hideout.
okText: The shadow slipped behind the tracker, put a knife to his ribs and took everything he had on him.

title: A guild thief
text: The thieves' guild has made it known that you work on their patch. Their man appeared on the roof.
okText: The shadow caught him in the dark and exchanged a few well-chosen words about territories.

title: Carrier pigeons
text: Carrier pigeons with other people's messages have started landing on your roof. Someone needs them badly.
okText: The marksman brought down a few pigeons with a flick of his sling and found interesting messages in the leg pouches.

title: A rooftop archer
text: Someone on the opposite roof is watching your windows. Whoever it is, he means no good.
okText: The marksman spotted him and put an arrow in the chimney by his head. The rooftop guest made a swift retreat.

title: Riot in the square
text: A crowd is gathering in a nearby square because the butchers' guild has quarrelled with the bakers'. No one is hurrying to calm it.
okText: The provocateur added fuel to the fire and while everyone went for each other, the followers had time to take what they could from the stalls.

title: The drunken lottery
text: The inn next door is running an illegal lottery. If the right man wins, there's good money to be made.
okText: The provocateur steered things so that someone from the crew won, and the innkeeper never worked out why.

title: The broken stove
text: The den's stove went out and the chimney collapsed. Without a good hand the crew will sleep in the cold.
okText: The scavenger put it all back together within an hour from salvaged bricks and old tin, even finding two old bars.

title: The wounded in the alley
text: Two wounded men lie in the next alley, one in a very bad way. Somebody must tend them before they bleed out on the doorstep.
okText: The scavenger dressed both wounds and was rewarded with a purse from one of them and a promise of a favour.

title: The night supplier
text: A river smuggler asks for a place to stash a few barrels for a night. Refusing is risky, and so is agreeing.
okText: The carter knew the smuggler and how to come out ahead: the barrels rested in the cellar and a decent fee was paid for hiding them.

title: The stranded wagon
text: Someone's wagon, with two wheels broken and a full load, got stuck outside your window. Someone will be looking for it in the morning.
okText: The carter fixed the wheels, hauled the wagon round the corner and took what he could before the owner came.

title: Crates on the corner
text: Someone left crates with flammable contents outside the tenement. One spark and half the street will go up.
okText: The arsonist recognised the contents and carefully moved the crates to a safe place, collecting a stock of oil and pitch on the way.

title: The shut gate
text: The merchants' guild has locked the gate to the granary. Someone in the crew wants in, but the lock is solid.
okText: The arsonist took off the hinges without a sound. The granary swung open and they carried off a week's supplies.

title: Chase across the roofs
text: Someone runs along the roofs above your heads, the watch behind him. His escape leads straight towards your home.
okText: The scout predicted the route and got the fugitive into the cellar while sending the guards the wrong way. The fugitive repaid him generously.

title: New chambers
text: A crack appeared in the cellar wall, revealing an old passage beyond. Nobody knows where it leads.
okText: The scout carefully explored the passage and found a forgotten cache with a few silver pieces and two emergency exits.

title: The false coin
text: A forged coin turned up in a follower's pocket. If anyone paid rent with it, there'd be trouble.
okText: The fence recognised the forger's craft, melted the coin into an ingot and got an honest price from the right dealer.

title: A dealer with suspicious goods
text: A stranger is offering a consignment at a price no one should ask. Either he's a great merchant or the goods are stolen.
okText: The fence inspected the goods, negotiated a sensible price and resold them at a decent profit.

title: A sick neighbour
text: Coughing and groaning come from the next flat. If it's the plague, the whole street will look for someone to blame.
okText: The healer looked in on the sick man, recognised an ordinary fever, gave herbs and calmed the neighbours, getting a few coppers in thanks.

title: Rumour of a witch
text: A rumour among the neighbours says a witch lives in your tenement. The hunters may knock soon.
okText: The healer appeared in the yard, handed out sprigs scented "from Sigmar" and told the neighbours his version so well they began paying for his protection.

title: A duel of honour
text: A tipsy noble challenged one of yours for a rude gesture. The challenge is serious, and the opponent too stubborn.
okText: The duellist stepped in, beat the noble without a scratch and gracefully returned his sword in exchange for a purse "as a keepsake".

title: Practice in the yard
text: Someone in the yard is challenging passers-by to fights for money. If a crewman gets involved it may bring a purse or a bruise.
okText: The duellist disarmed all comers in three moves and took the stakes while the crowd applauded.

title: A mysterious letter
text: A sealed letter with no addressee lies by the door in the morning. It seems to wait for someone to claim it.

title: The sender comes back
text: The man who left the letter came back and politely asks for it. He is nervous and pays for discretion.

title: The chest in the cellar
text: While cleaning the cellar a locked chest was found that no one remembers. There's no key, and the lock must be bypassed.

title: The chest's owner
text: An elderly man knocks and asks about a chest that belonged to his brother. He says his brother left for good.

title: The young runaway
text: A lad in a worn coat tumbled into the cellar by accident, running from someone. He begs to hide for one night.

title: The lad returns with thanks
text: The youngster returned with a bundle of food and a promise to speak only to those he trusts. His family has influence.

title: The corpse cart
text: A cart of bodies rolled down the street after the latest sickness. The driver looked away, but the stench lingered.

title: A Sigmarite procession
text: A procession of flagellants passed through the street, singing of the end of the world. Half the crew followed out of curiosity, the rest shut the shutters.

title: Hexenstag
text: On Hexenstag Eve people burn fires at street corners to ward off evil spirits. The crew built its own.

title: Market day
text: A great market in the city, crowds and uproar. Full pockets and empty pockets change hands.

title: The tax collector
text: The tax collector goes door to door with two guards. He didn't knock at your cellar, but the next one was hit with harsh penalties.

title: Militia recruitment
text: A recruiting sergeant is looking for young men for the city militia. Two of the crew pretended not to be there.

title: The tanners' guild
text: The tanners in the next district dumped their waste barrels into the river. The stench seeped all the way into your cellar.

title: The night digger
text: Someone has been digging underground nearby for two nights. Nobody knows if it's a ratcatcher, a sewer man or something worse.

title: The horse thief
text: A horse thief fled through the alley and abandoned his prize in your gateway. In the morning the horse stood quietly against the wall, regarding the crew.

title: Students from the university
text: A band of drunken students came down the alley singing bawdy songs. One lost his purse and another borrowed a follower's doublet.

title: The alchemist's smoking cauldron
text: On the next-door attic the alchemist has botched something again. The chimney smoke is green and the neighbours' windows are cracking one by one.

title: The hangman at the inn
text: The hangman spent an evening at the inn next door. Nobody wanted to sit near him, so everyone had more room.

title: The busy scribe
text: A clerk from the chancery rented a bed near your den and copied letters until dawn. He left behind an inkwell.

title: The broken gutter
text: A gutter on the roof cracked and water flooded one corner. The supplies had to be shifted somewhere dry.

title: The Tilean trader
text: A Tilean merchant stopped nearby, loud and generous. He handed out olives and tales of treasure.

title: The Dwarf smith
text: A Dwarf in the next lane woke the whole neighbourhood with his hammer. In the morning someone found freshly sharpened knives at the door.

title: The questioning
text: The watch led away a suspected forger from the tenement. They questioned everyone around, but passed you over.

title: The four merry widows
text: Four widows from the next street held a funeral for one's husband. It turned into a feast to which the crew was invited.

title: Flood on the Reik
text: The river burst its banks and flooded the waterside lanes. The cellar was spared, but supplies had to be moved.

title: Smoke from the workshop
text: A fire in a carpenter's workshop lit the sky. The watch was busy putting it out and the district slept soundly.

title: The dovecote
text: Someone keeps pigeons in the next tower. Their agitated cooing is heard every night, and in the morning a few had landed in your corner.

title: A brawl at the well
text: Two women fought over their turn at the well and doused each other. A crowd gathered and the pickpockets had a busy day.

title: The masterless dog
text: A big stray dog wandered up to the gate and fell asleep on the threshold. He scares anyone who tries to enter, even your own.

title: A warning from an informant
text: One of your old contacts sent a boy with a note: "Mind Thursday." Nobody knows what it means.

title: The craft fair
text: Artisans set up stalls along the whole street. The crew spotted a few items that could be bought or lifted.

title: The lost girl
text: A neighbour's child wandered into the cellar at night. She was taken back to her parents, who rewarded you with a few apples.

title: The high priest in town
text: A high-ranking priest has arrived in the city and the streets are patrolled doubly. The hideout had two unexpected visits.

title: The drunken barge
text: A barge of ale hit the quay and the barrels rolled down the ramp. Everyone gathered what they could while pretending to help.

title: The ratcatcher
text: A ratcatcher with strangely bright eyes offered his services. You grudgingly agreed to two nights of work, and by morning the cellar was quiet.

title: The ghost in the tenement
text: Someone saw a figure in a white shirt at the window. Probably a thief, but at midnight everyone preferred to watch their necks.

title: Smashed door
text: Someone is trying to break the door of your den in the middle of the night. Either he's very drunk or very desperate.
okText: The bodyguard opened the door and asked with a smile how he could help. The intruder paled and withdrew with apologies.

title: Shoving in the queue
text: A fight broke out in the bread queue and one of yours got involved. Without intervention he'll end up in the cells.
okText: The bodyguard parted the crowd like a ram, hauled his man out and "requisitioned" several loaves on the way.

title: The quiet visitor
text: Someone entered the hideout and vanished soundlessly with a sack. Supplies mysteriously shrank but nobody saw the thief.
okText: The shadow tracked the burglar to his lair, retrieved the sack and helped himself to something more from the thief's stash.

title: A strange face at the tavern
text: A stranger in the next inn asks too many questions about your crew. You must find out who he is.
okText: The shadow watched him till morning, saw him meet a shady type and quietly lifted a letter of instruction from him.

title: Crows
text: Crows settled on the roof and their racket is calling the guards. Someone must silence them as a patrol approaches with a lantern.
okText: The marksman silently brought down several birds from the roof and made a hearty soup of them for supper.

title: The enemy on the tower
text: Someone has taken the church tower opposite and has all your windows in view. He looks like a scout for a rival crew.
okText: The marksman lay in wait in a loft and sent an arrow into the bell from a distance. The stranger fled in a panic, leaving his pouch.

title: Rumour of plague
text: Someone at the market spread a rumour that sickness has broken out in your street. Merchants avoid the area, neighbours are afraid.
okText: The provocateur loudly dispelled the rumour at the inn and pointed out the real culprits, who paid for peace and quiet.

title: The heckling
text: A group of tipsy youths is harassing passers-by and approaching your gate. One of them has a belligerent look.
okText: The provocateur disarmed them with a joke, convinced them that free ale flowed in the next tavern and even got a few coins from them.

title: Spoiled supplies
text: Some of the supplies are starting to smell suspicious. If no one acts, everyone will have stomach cramps.
okText: The scavenger sorted the supplies, threw out the rotten and turned the rest into a spiced stew that tasted better than fresh.

title: A body in the gutter
text: The body of a stranger lies in the gutter outside the house. If nobody deals with it, it'll draw the watch.
okText: The scavenger dealt with the body and found a few coins and an interesting ring in the pockets. The corpse vanished down the sewer.

title: Street blockade
text: The watch blocked the street outside and is searching wagons. Your stores are in one of them.
okText: The carter knew the side alleys like his own pocket, brought the wagon round the back and even earned by renting space to other merchants.

title: The late smuggler
text: Your smuggler contact didn't show for the meeting, and your goods are waiting on the quay. The guards are beginning to take an interest.
okText: The carter arranged a substitute boat and a fake shipment, and the goods arrived with a bonus.

title: The powder keg
text: Someone left a keg of gunpowder in the next gateway under the neighbours' supervision. One stray spark and two streets vanish.
okText: The arsonist moved the keg to a safe place and emptied nearly half of it, tucking the powder into his own stash.

title: The leaking roof
text: A neighbour threatens to report your night visits to the watch if you don't repair his roof. He says you damaged it.
okText: The arsonist knew every weak point in the structure, convinced the neighbour that a patch would do and even earned his gratitude.

title: New routes
text: In the morning someone bricked up one of your exits and closed another. A new way must be found before you're trapped.
okText: The scout laid out three new routes through roofs and cellars in an hour and marked them with chalk visible only to his own.

title: The delivery
text: A man handed a courier a purse and pointed at your door. The courier vanished and soon someone began watching the entrance.
okText: The scout intercepted the courier before he reached his goal and took the parcel, which held a few letters and some coins.

title: The guild inspector
text: A merchants' guild inspector is coming down to the cellar because he heard of an unregistered warehouse. Without papers there will be a fine.
okText: The fence produced a pile of documents that looked more official than the seals themselves. The inspector apologised and left.

title: Buying the loot
text: An antiques dealer offers to buy some of your "finds" at a good price. The question is whether it isn't a trap.
okText: The fence investigated the buyer, checked his references and negotiated payment up front. The sale went through with interest.

title: Poisoning
text: Several followers complain of stomach pain after last night's supper. If nobody helps they'll go to a physician, who will ask questions.
okText: The healer gave a decoction of herbs, let a little blood from each and declared it "the antidote". Everyone felt better.

title: A beggar with a cough
text: A coughing beggar sat on your steps. Others pass by, and if he dies there'll be trouble.
okText: The healer poured a little of his own potion into him, collected a handful of coins from neighbours for the "miracle" and sent the beggar to a shelter.

title: The street fencer's challenge
text: A street fencer has challenged your men to a duel for precedence in the district. Losing would wreck the crew's standing.
okText: The crew's swashbuckler accepted the challenge and beat his rival without losing his roguish smile, and the onlookers tossed him coins.

title: An accidental insult
text: A guardsman is telling loud jokes about your crew. If no one reacts, the laughter will spread through the district.
okText: The swashbuckler replied with a quip the guard couldn't answer and won the respect of everyone present.

title: The wounded soldier
text: A wounded soldier in a bloodied uniform lies by the door. He mumbles about treachery and begs for shelter.

title: The pursuit of the soldier
text: Two men in unmarked cloaks ask after a wounded soldier. They promise good pay for information.

title: The strange barrel
text: A sealed barrel stands on the doorstep with the stamped crest of a foreign house. Nobody ordered it.

title: When they came back for the barrel
text: Four men with a crest on their sleeves turn up for the barrel. Nobody remembers who rolled it into the cellar.

title: The merchant family's trouble
text: A young merchant's wife came to you for advice: someone is blackmailing her husband. She promised silence and a small reward.

title: The blackmailer found
text: The man who blackmailed the merchant fell into the watch's hands. Before arrest he managed to blurt that someone from the crew helped him.

title: The street fiddler
text: A fiddler played under your window till dawn. Half the crew was furious, half danced.

title: The neighbours' feud
text: Two families across the yard quarrelled all night. Nobody heard your footsteps.

title: A lost key
text: Someone dropped the granary key and the crew found it. In the morning the owner promised a reward to whoever returns it.

title: Night ratting
text: Men with lanterns hunted rats in the alleys. The crew joined in and searched a few cellars on the way.

title: An ambiguous evening
text: A woman in a fine cloak knocked, asked directions and vanished. She left a trail of expensive perfume.

title: The fortune teller
text: A market fortune teller told one follower of a long life and a great loss. Nobody knows if that's good news.

title: A window on the world
text: Someone smashed a window next door and ran off with chests. The watch was busy investigating and you had a quiet night.

title: The missionary of Sigmar
text: A young priest of Sigmar stopped nearby and preached on the corner. Nobody listened but coins landed in his bowl.

title: A noble's bastard
text: A youth with suspiciously noble features asks the way to your district. He looks like a child born on the wrong side of the blanket.

title: Theft from a stall
text: Lads from your circle swiped a basket of fruit from a stall and hid it in the cellar. The trader is looking for them.

title: Fire at the inn
text: A barrel of oil burst at the inn around the corner. The innkeeper raised the alarm and regulars had to be rescued.

title: Armed men on the street
text: Armed men in the colours of some family walked the street in silence. They were looking for something, but not your door.

title: Street urchins
text: Street urchins brought a handful of news and asked for bread in return. The news was worth the price.

title: Snow
text: The first snow covered the streets. Fewer footsteps in the city, and the chimney smokes less than it should.

title: The lost raven
text: A raven without feet flew to the window and stared at the crew for an hour. Then it left as if it had understood everything.

title: Masquerade
text: A masquerade is held in the district and the streets are full of masks. One can get lost, or one can earn.

title: The sleeping guard
text: A guard fell asleep at your gate with a tankard in hand. In the morning he woke ashamed and left a quarter-shilling.

title: The banner
text: A military banner marched through the city with drums and trumpets. Children ran after it and adults hid their valuables.

title: Screams from the tenement
text: Screams came from the second floor opposite. When they finally stopped, nobody dared to check.

title: The toppled lantern
text: A street lantern fell and went out. In the dark someone slipped down an alley that was previously lit.

title: An old friend
text: A former companion from another crew knocked. You reminisced and he left with a heavy head and a lighter purse.

title: The great cheese quarrel
text: Two cheese sellers quarrelled over a spot and both landed in the river. Everyone had a laugh and the cheeses lay scattered in the street.

title: The burnt chapel
text: A small chapel burned in the night. People whispered of arson and looked for culprits among strangers.

title: The burgomaster on the street
text: The burgomaster passed through the district with his retinue and the crew hid everything that might arouse suspicion.

title: An item for sale
text: One of the followers found a strange figurine in the rubbish. A dealer bought it for three shillings and smiled knowingly.

title: Chimney smoke
text: All the chimneys in the district smoked at once because the night was frosty. One of them smoked thicker than the others.

title: The stone head
text: While digging out the cellar a stone head with an unknown symbol was found. Everyone fears it, but nobody threw it away.

title: The Shallyan mission
text: Sisters of Shallya hand out bread and medicine in the district. Your people got their share too.

title: The stray bear
text: A travelling menagerie lost its bear. The animal slept under your window until the keeper found it.

title: A debt of honour
text: An old companion came with a drunken band for an "overdue debt" the crew doesn't remember. He threatens to smash the door.
okText: The bodyguard stepped out and suggested settling it "man to man". The companion quickly remembered it was a mistake.

title: Escort for a merchant
text: A merchant in a cloak at the door asks for an escort to the city gate. He fears robbery and pays generously for fear.
okText: The bodyguard walked the merchant with such a look that no thug dared approach. The pay came with interest.

title: Thieves' signs
text: Someone is chalking marks on your door. For some it's an invitation, for others a sentence.
okText: The shadow recognised the guild's marks and added a note of his own that made thieves avoid the area, and they paid for the note.

title: Night flight
text: A man in a black cloak leaps across the roofs with someone behind him. He crashes into your cellar.
okText: The shadow took over, hid the fugitive and led the pursuit astray. The fugitive turned out to owe a noble and paid up.

title: The lost falcon
text: A falcon with a hood and bell perched on the roof. Someone is looking for it and will reward the finder generously.
okText: The marksman lured the bird with a scrap of meat and returned it to its owner, a wealthy merchant.

title: The butcher
text: A drunken butcher accuses your people of stealing hams. He demands compensation.
okText: The marksman bet the butcher on a shot at a hanging ham and hit exactly the marked spot. The butcher laughed, withdrew the accusation and threw in another ham.

title: Two merchants
text: Two merchants quarrel loudly over goods one didn't deliver. If someone doesn't begin mediation a fight will break out.
okText: The provocateur "settled" the dispute so that both merchants paid him for help, each thinking he had won.

title: Theatre evening
text: A travelling troupe performs on the street and the crowd is amused and generous. If someone sneaked onto the stage...
okText: The provocateur slipped into the play, did a turn as a drunken knight and took more from the hat than the whole troupe that night.

title: Clogged gutters
text: The gutters clogged after a storm and water is seeping into the cellar. They must be cleared or the storeroom floods.
okText: The scavenger cleared the gutters in a few moments and found a handful of small coins and a bit of silver chain in the muck.

title: The forgotten stockroom
text: The owner of the next tenement died and left a storeroom full of junk. The son wants to throw everything out tomorrow morning.
okText: The scavenger managed to sift through everything that very night and found several things fit for sale or for eating.

title: The onion cart
text: An onion merchant asks you to keep his cart for a night because his stable burned. Someone might look under the onions.
okText: The carter understood what was under the onions, took his fee for silence and saw that the cart left without trouble.

title: The stowaway
text: A stranger slept in your wagon and now won't get out. He says he's in debt and needs to leave the city.
okText: The carter took him through the gate in a barrel and was paid in gold the fugitive couldn't take with him.

title: The undermined wall
text: The wall of the tenement opposite collapsed after the rain, exposing the cellars. Barrels of something valuable can be seen inside.
okText: The arsonist examined the structure and made the rest of the wall collapse in the right direction, revealing all the barrels without a bang.

title: The informer neighbour
text: The neighbour below gathers evidence against the crew. He has a stack of letters and papers in his flat.
okText: The arsonist set his flat alight so that the papers burned and the fire was put out before anyone saw it.

title: The lost map
text: Someone left a map of the sewers at your door. It might be real or a trap.
okText: The scout checked the map in the field and it turned out to lead to an old hidden entrance to a merchant's strongroom.

title: The rumour of treasure
text: The inn whispers of treasure hidden under an old chapel. Many search, nobody has found it.
okText: The scout followed the only good lead, found the cache and brought a few golden items to the hideout.

title: The absconding debtor
text: A debtor borrowed from you at interest and now won't repay. He says he has no money but sizeable debts elsewhere.
okText: The fence bought the debtor's other debts for pennies, merged them with yours and collected it all from his wealthy family.

title: The new document
text: The watch demands a safe-conduct from everyone in the district. Yours are invalid and the penalty is harsh.
okText: The fence produced new papers with perfect seals that survived inspection, and the inspector praised their calligraphy.

title: A potion for aches
text: An elderly woman asks for an elixir for rheumatism with a queue behind her. If you have none, you lose the clientele.
okText: The healer pulled a bottle of "mandrake" potion (chamomile and vodka) from his bag and sold it to the whole queue.

title: The whisperer
text: An old whisperer visits the crew claiming she sees death on your faces. Some believe it.
okText: The healer whispered something in her ear, handed her a coin and told the crew it was an omen of long life. Calm returned.

title: The ball invitation
text: A young noblewoman asks one of yours to accompany her to a ball because her fiancé fell ill. Opportunity or trap.
okText: The duellist shone in the dance, won the guests' respect and came back with pockets full of small gifts and a few useful addresses.

title: A stab in the back
text: A rival crew staged an ambush in a blind alley. By the time you realise, it'll be too late.
okText: The duellist spotted the trap at the last moment, stepped out first with sabre in hand and demanded a duel. The opponents scattered.

title: The courier's visit
text: A courier from another crew leaves a message: "Let's meet, there's business." He didn't sign.

title: The meeting in the dark alley
text: A stranger comes to the agreed place with a map and a proposal. He wants a joint job on the guild warehouses and pays well for entry.

title: The strange coin
text: A follower shows a coin a stranger gave him. It bears an odd mark nobody recognises.

title: The mark returns
text: The mark from the coin appeared on the doors of several houses nearby. Someone is marking victims.

title: The curious guest
text: A wandering scholar knocks and asks for a night's lodging in exchange for stories. He looks exhausted.

title: The scholar returns
text: The scholar left in the morning but came back with a merchant who wants to buy a favour. He promises payment in silver.

title: The threats
text: A dead rat was left at the door with a note pinned: "I know what you do." The handwriting is crude.

title: The author reveals himself
text: The author of the note turned out to be a drunken merchant who thought you were another crew. He apologises and offers compensation.

title: The burning sign
text: Someone burned a hand-shaped symbol into your door. Nobody can read it.

title: The symbol explained
text: An old beggar says it's the sign of an old brotherhood that protected the neighbourhood. If you honour it you'll find allies.

title: Fog off the river
text: Thick fog crept in from the Reik. You couldn't see your hand before your face and every sound seemed strangely near.

title: The alarm bell
text: A bell rang the alarm in the night but nobody knew why. Half the district stood in the street in their nightshirts.

title: The lost woman
text: A woman without shoes sat at your gate and couldn't remember where she came from. The watch took her in the morning.

title: Smoke and scent
text: The smell of burnt herbs hung in the air. Somewhere nearby someone was performing a rite you didn't want to know about.

title: New prices
text: Merchants raised prices by a quarter after rumours of war. Your supplies melt faster than usual.

title: Hard frost
text: Frost turned the puddles to stone. Chimneys smoke and people round the fire swap tales of old times.

title: The uncle's visit
text: One follower's uncle dropped by with a basket of apples and accusations. After an hour everyone had had enough, but the apples stayed.

title: The new neighbour
text: A quiet man with a worn face moved into the empty flat. All day he never came out once.

title: The runaway horse
text: A horse broke its harness, ran through the district and stopped under your windows. Nobody claimed it.

title: The sewer man's joke
text: A sewer worker emerged from the hatch with a few jokes and a very strong smell. The followers laughed all night.

title: A noble in the market
text: A noble threw coins into the crowd for fun. Everybody dived and so did you.

title: The stolen ring
text: Someone abandoned a crested ring on your stairs. Somebody is surely looking for it.

title: Sigmar's day
text: All bells rang in honour of Sigmar. The streets were clean and the watch more alert than usual.

title: The night bookseller
text: A trader with a cart of forbidden books asked if anyone wanted "something interesting". He'd rather lose money than keep them.

title: The puppet show
text: A puppeteer staged a show for children while adults stood behind and listened. It carried more hints at your trade than anyone liked.

title: The bounty hunter
text: A bounty hunter asked about someone in your district. The description matched a man from the next tenement, but somebody felt uneasy.

title: The fishing boat
text: A fishing boat moored at the quay and fishermen gave out yesterday's catch to lighten their load. The crew didn't refuse.

title: A message from an informant
text: An old informant left a note with one sentence: "Big shipment tomorrow morning on the east quay." It can be used.

title: Wind
text: A strong wind roared over the city and tore off roof tiles. Nobody could sleep but the streets were empty.

title: The evening market
text: The last traders folded their stalls and sold the leftovers for pennies. The crew did the shopping of a lifetime.

title: The priests' quarrel
text: A priest of Sigmar and a priest of Ulric quarrelled publicly over a spot for a procession. The crowd was better entertained than at a fair.

title: The sound in the wall
text: Something has been knocking rhythmically in the cellar wall since yesterday. A rat, a pipe or a walled-in neighbour, nobody knows.

title: The old wayfarer
text: A grey-bearded traveller asked for water. He got it and in return told a tale of an old vault beneath the city.

title: Rotten apples
text: Someone left a crate of rotten apples at the door, as a warning or just by chance. The smell lingered all night.

title: Twelve blind men
text: Twelve blind beggars walked down the street in a line, each with a hand on the shoulder of the one before. It looked eerie.

title: The twins
text: Two followers turned out to be twin brothers separated in childhood. A touching reunion and a few interesting stories besides.

title: The lady next door
text: A pretty lady from next door struck up a conversation with a follower. When she left, his belt pouch was gone.

title: The watch parade
text: The city watch marched through the district with drums. In the ranks one seemed to recognise you.

title: Thunderstorm
text: Lightning hit the church tower and the bells sounded by themselves. People whispered of an omen.

title: The knife dealer
text: A knife seller at the gate offered weapons at a bargain price. He had few questions and so did you.

title: The talking parrots
text: Someone in the neighbourhood keeps parrots that repeat everything they hear. The district has learned to speak more quietly.

title: A bastard in church
text: During mass a child loudly shouted its father's name. The whole church went silent and one of the men turned white as chalk.

title: The cake riddle
text: A baker baked a cake with a coin inside. The crew ate it and the coin went to the one who needed it least.

title: The travelling circus
text: A travelling circus pitched tents on a vacant square. Half the district watched acrobats while the other half searched for lost purses.

title: The priest of Morr
text: A priest of Morr walked down the street at night carrying a black staff, a boy with a lantern behind him. The crew held its breath until they vanished.

title: The rat king
text: The rats in the cellar move in a strangely organised way. Some followers whisper of a rat king.

title: Trouble with the neighbour
text: The neighbour above emptied slops from the window onto a follower's shoulder. A quarrel began and ended with apologies and bread.

title: The collector
text: A collector raised funds to fix a chapel roof and an hour later it turned out there was no chapel. The money vanished with him.

title: The carriage race
text: Two carriages raced through the district and one crashed into your gate. The passengers were more shaken than hurt.

title: The hanging laundry
text: Laundry strung across the street blotted out an entire alley. Under the sheets slipped people unseen from below.

title: The crying baby
text: A baby cried the whole night in the next flat. In the morning the mother handed out bread by way of apology.

title: The Kislevite merchant
text: A Kislevite merchant stopped nearby and handed out furs for warmth. The cold was unbearable so everyone accepted.

title: The loan
text: A merchant offered a loan on very attractive terms. Too attractive to be true.

title: Smoke from the tavern
text: The tavern around the corner sent up the smell of roasting meat. Half the crew turned up there before sunrise.

title: The boy with a purse
text: A country boy came to the city with a purse of money seeking work. He looks lost and easy to cheat.

title: The country father
text: A weather-beaten man comes looking for his son. He says the son took all the savings from home.

title: The odd parcel
text: A parcel wrapped in black cloth lies on your doorstep. Nobody has the nerve to open it.

title: The parcel's contents
text: The parcel was finally opened. Inside lay a small silver statuette and a note with one line: "For the proper recipient."

title: The fox in the cellar
text: Scuffling comes from the cellar. Peering in, a follower saw a fox holding a piece of sausage.

title: The fox returns
text: The fox came back, this time with its whole family. Nobody has the heart to drive them off but the supplies vanish faster than usual.

title: The stranger with a violin
text: A street fiddler with a case wrapped in rags asks for shelter. He says someone threatens him because of the fiddle.

title: The fiddle's value
text: It turned out the fiddle is worth far more than it looks. A collector offers a huge sum but the fiddler has vanished.

title: The dark alley
text: Someone spilled tar on the cobbles and several passers-by stuck to the road. A chance for a few brilliant thefts.

title: News from the capital
text: A messenger brought word from the imperial court: whoever knows what it says could call in a great favour.

title: The wounded dog
text: A lame dog dragged itself into the cellar and looked sadly at everyone. Someone dressed its wound and fed it, and the dog didn't leave.

title: The hunted thief
text: A thief fleeing the watch tossed his loot through your window. Before anyone understood, he was gone.

title: A scream in the night
text: In the middle of the night a scream rang out and then silence. By morning all the windows in the neighbourhood were tightly shut.

title: The paying neighbourhood
text: The neighbours pooled money to fix the shared roof and politely asked if you would too. You have to pay or there'll be trouble.

title: The door without a handle
text: Someone removed the handle from your door in the night. In the morning you had to climb in through the window.

title: A ghost story
text: An elderly neighbour told a tale of the ghost of the cellar's previous tenant. Everyone listened and then nobody wanted to be alone.

title: A talk through the wall
text: Through the wall you can hear two men discussing a plan. From what could be understood it's a raid on a gold transport.

title: A good sleep
text: Everyone slept well, nobody had nightmares and nobody woke with a headache. It rarely happens.

title: The broken windlass
text: The well windlass broke and half the neighbourhood had to draw water from your yard. You collected a few thanks.

title: The curfew
text: The guards declared a curfew after dusk. The crew sat in the den, angry at the whole world.

title: The stray sheep
text: A sheep ran into the tenement and froze on the stairs. The lads stole it before the owner could claim it.

title: Drinking at the inn
text: A drinking bout is on at the inn next door and the noise goes through every wall. Those who wanted to sleep can forget it.

title: The farrier
text: A smith from the next street invited people to see his work. The crew bought a few horseshoes and let him tell the story of his life.

title: The missing cat
text: Children are looking for a missing cat. One looked into your cellar and saw things he shouldn't have.

title: The bathhouse
text: The city bathhouse announced a free-entry day. The crew turned up in full and came back clean as a whistle.

title: Changing the guard
text: The watch changed the post on your street. The new men don't know the area yet and their eyes shine with zeal.

title: The medicine chest
text: A chest of medicines fell from a wagon and some phials smashed on the cobbles. The rest found their way into your hands.

title: Sounds from the roof
text: Someone walked on the roof all night. Nobody moved to check and in the morning there were only a few pigeon feathers on the roof.

title: The funeral procession
text: A rich merchant's funeral went down the street in full pomp. One of the mourners had a suspiciously light purse on his return.

title: A sharp stench
text: A terrible stench drifts from the sewer. The sewer workers claim it's normal but everyone feels something has died.

title: The doctor's visit
text: The city physician went through the houses recording the sick. You were put on the list of the healthy, a rare mark of favour.

title: The chased-off beggar
text: A guard drove a beggar from your gate. The beggar came back an hour later and told you what he saw in the next house.

title: A mouse in the kitchen
text: A mouse ate half a loaf and the cat that was supposed to catch it ate the other half. Less and less food remains.

title: The Tilean singers
text: Travelling Tilean singers gave a concert at the street corner. The crowd was generous and the pickpockets more so.

title: Cabbages
text: A cart of cabbages overturned outside. People rushed to gather them and forgot their dignity.

title: The wall graffiti
text: Someone painted an insulting drawing of the burgomaster on a wall during the night. The watch began a search and you were in good spirits.

title: The two brothers
text: Two brothers from the neighbourhood argued over an inheritance and one threw a chair at the other. Everybody watched from the windows.

title: The confession
text: A priest of Shallya heard a follower's confession and he returned visibly lighter and very thoughtful.

title: A red sky
text: The sunset was strangely red and lingered long. Old folk said it was a bad hour for any business.

title: The clever girl
text: The laundress's girl recognised one follower and threatened to go to the watch unless she got crowns.

title: A friend's funeral
text: An old friend of the crew died. He was buried with honours and some money was collected for his family.

title: Free ale
text: A brewery held a tasting of its new ale and gave out several barrels. The followers returned merry with tankards under their arms.

title: The ratcatchers' parade
text: The ratcatchers' guild paraded a cart full of dead rats through the streets in a ceremonial procession. Everyone looked disgusted.

title: The boy with a letter
text: A boy with a letter looked for an addressee nobody knows. He left the letter with you and ran off.

title: The snowstorm
text: A blizzard buried the streets and erased all tracks. The watch was busy clearing snow and nobody looked for anybody.

title: The wager
text: Two followers bet on who'd catch a rat first. The winner got a quarter-shilling, the loser laughter.

title: The woman with a jug
text: An elderly woman with a jug of milk comes every day. Today she gave two jugs for free because "you're so thin."

title: The unsolicited advice
text: An old soldier with a wooden leg gave the young followers advice on fighting. Half was good, half invented.

title: The priest's visit
text: A priest knocked asking for support for an almshouse. He received a few shillings and promised to pray for the whole crew's souls.

title: A friend of a friend
text: A stranger says "a friend of a friend" sent him and asks for a small favour. He won't give a name.

title: The price of a favour
text: The man came back with a gift in thanks. It turns out he has influence in the merchants' guild and promises to remember the crew.

title: The dump under the window
text: Someone dumped a pile of junk under your window and something glints in it. The owner will probably return in the morning.

title: The owner of the junk
text: A man with a handcart came and demanded the return of a "stolen" thing. It's unclear what he means but he was furious.

title: The craftsman in need
text: A carpenter from the next lane asks to borrow a few crowns for materials. He promises to repay with interest.

title: The debt repaid
text: The carpenter came back with the whole sum plus interest and a box of his own making as a gift. His neighbours began to ask for your help too.

title: Morrslieb in the sky
text: The greenish moon Morrslieb hung low over the rooftops. Dogs howled and a few followers wouldn't step over the threshold.

title: Witch Hunters in the district
text: Witch Hunters went through the district with torches, dragging people from their homes. The crew sat quiet as mice until they left.

title: The sign of the Purple Hand
text: A painted purple handprint appeared on the wall of the next house. By morning it was gone, but people wouldn't walk past it.

title: The press-gang
text: Armed men from a ship snatched several drunks from the street for barge service. Your people hid in the cellar and waited it out.

title: A shrine of Ranald
text: Someone built a small shrine to Ranald in the alley with a few coins at its foot. Everyone took it for a good sign.

title: The influential guest
text: A clerk from the burgomaster's office moved into the next tenement. The area suddenly became cleaner and more watchful.

title: The Verenan court
text: Judges passed down the street with a retinue, servants with books going before them, and everyone they passed doffed a cap.

title: The wizard on the roof
text: Someone in a black robe sat on the neighbouring roof gazing at the stars. Nobody dared ask what he was looking for.

title: The vanished neighbour
text: An elderly neighbour never came back from a night errand. His door stood open and the cat sat on the sill staring into emptiness.

title: A new burgomaster
text: It was proclaimed that a new burgomaster takes office. For a day chaos reigned, which the crew cleverly exploited.

title: Dirty water
text: The district well turned murky and foul. Everyone drank ale and the crew sold a few barrels at a good price.

title: The lost signet
text: Your man lost a signet bearing the crew's emblem in a drunken brawl. If it falls into the wrong hands it could cause trouble.

title: The merchant in debt
text: A well-known merchant in debt jumped from a window and smashed on the cobbles outside your house. Someone counted what he left behind.

title: The travelling troupe
text: A travelling troupe of actors staged a play on the street about noble outlaws. The crew watched intently and some even shed a tear.

title: The missing child
text: A neighbourhood child vanished at night. The whole street searched with lanterns and found it sleeping in your cellar.

title: The night mass
text: A night mass was held in the next chapel with many attending. Everyone left in silence and some wept.

title: The baker in debt
text: The baker fell behind on payments and sought support. You took him under your wing and got fresh bread for a week.

title: The barrel of wine
text: A barrel of wine rolled down a steep alley and stopped right at your door. Nobody knows where it came from.

title: The watchtower
text: The entire shift of guards vanished from the watchtower. The watch seeks culprits and the district whispers of treachery.

title: The open window
text: The window of one house stood open all night with a candle burning inside. By morning it turned out the house had been empty for years.

title: The family recipe
text: One follower's grandmother visited and brought a cake from a recipe passed down through generations. Everyone ate it to the last crumb.

title: The new wanted poster
text: A wanted notice bearing one follower's likeness appeared on the notice board. The artist had no talent, which is probably why nobody recognised him.

title: Nine shillings
text: Nine shillings lay in the gutter. Nobody moved, each waiting for someone else to bend first. You were quicker.
